title: Inside the Five Days That Remade the Supreme Court

sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在凌晨4点半给总统打了电话，他接听了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 七十年的太空探索。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗恒星之外有什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费者产品指南。

sentences.zh: 今天我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60份超级圣代。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》，庆祝175年来帮助您了解世界并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 现在订阅可享受特别优惠，网址是nytimes.com斜杠subscribe。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日简报》。

sentences.en: For the past decade, the Supreme Court has relied on a rushed and secretive system to make major rulings on everything from immigration to presidential power.
sentences.zh: 在过去十年里，最高法院一直依赖一套仓促且保密的系统，对从移民到总统权力等一切重大事项做出裁决。

sentences.en: Now, for the first time, a Times investigation brings to light the precise moment when that system began.
sentences.zh: 现在，《纽约时报》的一项调查首次揭示了该系统开始的确切时刻。

sentences.en: Today, Jodi Kantor and Adam Liptak take us inside the five days that we made the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 今天，乔迪·坎托和亚当·利普塔克带我们深入了解了我们塑造最高法院的那五天。

sentences.en: Monday, April 20th.
sentences.zh: 4月20日，星期一。

sentences.en: Jodi, Adam, together at last in one episode of The Daily.
sentences.zh: 乔迪，亚当，终于在《每日简报》的一期节目中聚首了。

sentences.en: Thank you for being here.
sentences.zh: 感谢你们来到这里。

sentences.en: Great to be with you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能和你在一起。

sentences.en: It's good to be here, Michael.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里，迈克尔。

sentences.en: So you two joined forces for an investigation that seems to begin with a genuine curiosity, which is, what are the origins of the Supreme Court's shadow docket?
sentences.zh: 所以你们俩联手进行了一项调查，这似乎始于一个真正的好奇心，那就是，最高法院“影子案卷”的起源是什么？

sentences.en: So tell us why you were both drawn to answering that question.
sentences.zh: 那么告诉我们，为什么你们俩都想回答这个问题。

sentences.en: It's a pretty common sense question, Michael, because if we look at the court's rulings, they are doing an enormous amount of work on the shadow docket.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常合乎常理的问题，迈克尔，因为如果我们看看法院的裁决，他们正在“影子案卷”上做大量的工作。

sentences.en: These are really important rulings that bypass a lot of the time-tested steps of the court.
sentences.zh: 这些是非常重要的裁决，绕过了法院许多久经考验的步骤。

sentences.en: So part of what we're asking here is, let's go back to the beginning.
sentences.zh: 所以我们在这里提出的部分问题是，让我们回到最初。

sentences.en: How did the court start doing this?
sentences.zh: 法院是怎么开始这么做的？

sentences.en: Where does this come from?
sentences.zh: 这从何而来？

sentences.en: Adam, I know we've talked on the show about the shadow docket quite a bit, but just remind us what it is, and more importantly, how, as Jodi just said,
sentences.zh: 亚当，我知道我们在节目中已经谈论过很多次“影子案卷”了，但请提醒我们它是什么，更重要的是，正如乔迪刚才所说，

sentences.en: it bypasses the time-tested steps of the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 它是如何绕过最高法院久经考验的步骤的。

sentences.en: So a good way to think about this is to contrast it with the usual way the court handles cases.
sentences.zh: 所以，考虑这个问题的一个好方法是将其与法院处理案件的通常方式进行对比。

sentences.en: Lawyers call this the court's merits docket, and this is what we're kind of used to.
sentences.zh: 律师们称之为法院的“案情案卷”，这就是我们比较习惯的那种。

sentences.en: The justices spend a lot of time considering which cases they're going to hear, and they get briefs on that.
sentences.zh: 大法官们花大量时间考虑他们要审理哪些案件，并为此获取案情摘要。

sentences.en: And if they decide to hear a case, they get another round of briefs and supporting briefs, and then they hear arguments, and then they sit together and discuss and vote.
sentences.zh: 如果他们决定审理一个案件，他们会收到另一轮摘要和支持性摘要，然后他们听取辩论，接着坐在一起讨论并投票。

sentences.en: And then they exchange drafts, 5, 10, 15 drafts of opinions and concurrences and dissents.
sentences.zh: 然后他们交换草稿，5份、10份、15份意见书、协同意见书和异议书的草稿。

sentences.en: And after all this process winds itself out for like a year, they issue a reasoned decision, could be 100 pages long,
sentences.zh: 在所有这些程序持续大约一年后，他们会发布一份有理有据的裁决，可能长达100页，

sentences.en: with lots of concurrences and dissents, and it's the product of great care and deliberation.
sentences.zh: 附带大量的协同意见书和异议书，这是精心审议的产物。

sentences.en: And these decisions, of course, are law that binds the nation, it gives guidance to lower courts, tells litigants how they have to act.
sentences.zh: 当然，这些裁决是约束全国的法律，为下级法院提供指导，告诉诉讼当事人他们必须如何行事。

sentences.en: That's the Supreme Court we're used to.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们习惯的最高法院。

sentences.en: The shadow docket short-circuits all of that.
sentences.zh: “影子案卷”绕过了所有这些。

sentences.en: It happens in a very brief period of time on thin briefs, no arguments, no in-person deliberations.
sentences.zh: 它在很短的时间内发生，基于简略的摘要，没有辩论，没有当面审议。

sentences.en: It gives rise to rulings with scant or no reasoning at all.
sentences.zh: 它产生的裁决理由很少，甚至根本没有理由。

sentences.en: And over the past 10 years, this has really become a major part of the court's business,
sentences.zh: 在过去10年里，这确实已成为法院工作的主要部分，

sentences.en: including in some decisions over the past year or so that have awarded President Trump enormous leeway and power.
sentences.zh: 包括过去一年左右的一些裁决，这些裁决赋予了特朗普总统巨大的回旋余地和权力。

sentences.en: Increasingly, the court has turned to this shadow docket.
sentences.zh: 法院越来越多地转向这种“影子案卷”。

sentences.en: This is an exponential increase in the Supreme Court's use of the shadow docket, more than anything we have ever seen before.
sentences.zh: 这是最高法院使用“影子案卷”的指数级增长，比我们以前见过的任何情况都要多。

sentences.en: They've used it 20 times so far this year, and the year's not even over yet.
sentences.zh: 今年到目前为止他们已经使用了20次，而且这一年还没过完呢。

sentences.en: It's insane at the shadow docket.
sentences.zh: “影子案卷”太疯狂了。

sentences.en: And what critics have worried about is they've said...
sentences.zh: 批评者担心的是，他们说……

sentences.en: The race to create fait accompli is changing the speed and rhythm of all of these cases.
sentences.zh: 制造既成事实的竞赛正在改变所有这些案件的速度和节奏。

sentences.en: Why is the Supreme Court not moving at its usual careful, deliberate pace?
sentences.zh: 为什么最高法院没有按照其通常谨慎、审慎的步伐前进？

sentences.en: There's no problem in the abstract with the idea that the Supreme Court gets emergencies.
sentences.zh: 抽象地讲，最高法院处理紧急情况的想法本身没有问题。

sentences.en: The problem we've seen in the last five or six years is the way the justices are intervening.
sentences.zh: 我们在过去五六年里看到的问题是大法官们干预的方式。

sentences.en: And also...
sentences.zh: 还有……

sentences.en: You get this kind of back-of-the-envelope reasoning from the justices two, three sentences.
sentences.zh: 你从大法官那里得到这种草率的推理，只有两三句话。

sentences.en: Those decisions are not reasoned decisions.
sentences.zh: 这些裁决不是有理有据的裁决。

sentences.en: They don't tell us why.
sentences.zh: 他们没有告诉我们原因。

sentences.en: I mean, five paragraphs doesn't tell us why.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，五段话并不能说明原因。

sentences.en: Why is the Supreme Court not providing any reasoning for such major decisions?
sentences.zh: 为什么最高法院对如此重大的裁决不提供任何理由？

sentences.en: But the emergency docket or shadow docket is a dangerous thing.
sentences.zh: 但紧急案卷或“影子案卷”是一件危险的事情。

sentences.en: You run to the court.
sentences.zh: 你冲向法院。

sentences.en: You don't have full briefing.
sentences.zh: 你没有完整的案情摘要。

sentences.en: You don't have full argument.
sentences.zh: 你没有完整的辩论。

sentences.en: So critics have been concerned both about the quality of the rulings.
sentences.zh: 所以批评者既担心裁决的质量。

sentences.en: Is it possible to issue a really solid ruling in such a shortened process?
sentences.zh: 在如此缩短的程序中，有可能做出真正扎实的裁决吗？

sentences.en: And also the lack of communication with the public?
sentences.zh: 也担心与公众缺乏沟通？

sentences.en: Right, because these rapidly reached, barely explained rulings that emerge from the shadow docket raise a really important question.
sentences.zh: 没错，因为这些从“影子案卷”中产生的、仓促达成且几乎没有解释的裁决，提出了一个非常重要的问题。

sentences.en: Is the country's highest court rushing to rule based on, because we don't really know, gut instinct, personal peak, partisan instinct, all the things that a slow, deliberate,
sentences.zh: 这个国家最高法院是否在基于——因为我们并不真正知道——直觉、个人偏见、党派本能，以及所有一个缓慢、审慎的、

sentences.en: judicious system is meant to avoid?
sentences.zh: 公正的系统旨在避免的事情而仓促做出裁决？

sentences.en: We don't know.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道。

sentences.en: Well, defenders of the shadow docket, the emergency docket, will say a couple of things.
sentences.zh: 嗯，“影子案卷”即紧急案卷的捍卫者会说几件事。

sentences.en: One is that these kinds of orders have a long history, and that's true.
sentences.zh: 一是这类命令有悠久的历史，这是事实。

sentences.en: The court has often interceded when it needs to move very fast,
sentences.zh: 法院经常在需要非常迅速行动时进行干预，

sentences.en: like in a death penalty case when someone's about to be put to death or an election dispute where you need to know by Tuesday what the answer is.
sentences.zh: 比如在死刑案件中，当有人即将被处决时，或者在选举纠纷中，你需要到周二就知道答案是什么。

sentences.en: And also occasionally in discrete areas like abortion, the court has issued emergency orders, but it's not used the emergency docket to address major national policy initiatives.
sentences.zh: 此外，偶尔在堕胎等离散领域，法院也发布过紧急命令，但它并没有利用紧急案卷来处理重大的国家政策倡议。

sentences.en: The second thing I'd say, or the defenders of these orders would say, is that they're temporary.
sentences.zh: 我要说的第二点，或者说这些命令的捍卫者会说，它们是暂时的。

sentences.en: They're not meant to conclusively resolve the case.
sentences.zh: 它们不是为了最终解决案件。

sentences.en: They're just holding the status quo while the case moves to the lower courts, comes back to the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 它们只是在案件移交下级法院、回到最高法院的过程中维持现状。

sentences.en: So they're nominally temporary, but as a practical matter, very often they're not only consequential but conclusive, finally resolving the matter.
sentences.zh: 所以它们名义上是暂时的，但实际上，它们往往不仅具有后果，而且是决定性的，最终解决了问题。

sentences.en: Because if the court says you can deport someone or you can deport hundreds of thousands of people or you can withhold aid money or you can fire thousands of people.
sentences.zh: 因为如果法院说你可以驱逐某人，或者你可以驱逐成千上万的人，或者你可以扣留援助资金，或者你可以解雇成千上万的人。

sentences.en: You're talking about shadow docket cases of the Trump era.
sentences.zh: 你指的是特朗普时代的“影子案卷”案件。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: These are not hypotheticals.
sentences.zh: 这些不是假设。

sentences.en: These are actual cases.
sentences.zh: 这些是实际的案件。

sentences.en: Those are very hard to undo.
sentences.zh: 那些很难撤销。

sentences.en: You can say it's temporary.
sentences.zh: 你可以说它是暂时的。

sentences.en: But if they imagine it goes back to the court and imagine the court says, you know what, actually the Trump administration was wrong, it's very hard to undo those rulings.
sentences.zh: 但如果他们想象它回到法院，想象法院说，你知道吗，实际上特朗普政府错了，撤销这些裁决是非常困难的。

sentences.en: So even if they are temporary in nature, they are extremely meaningful in practice.
sentences.zh: 所以即使它们本质上是暂时的，它们在实践中也极具意义。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so the question is, what is actually happening inside the Supreme Court with these cases?
sentences.zh: 所以问题是，最高法院内部在这些案件上到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: And Adam and I wanted to see if we could find out.
sentences.zh: 亚当和我想要看看我们是否能找到答案。

sentences.en: And we did.
sentences.zh: 我们做到了。

sentences.en: And what does that very tantalizing sentence actually mean?
sentences.zh: 那句非常诱人的话到底是什么意思？

sentences.en: You did.
sentences.zh: 你们做到了。

sentences.en: Well, the New York Times has obtained and has published 16 pages of confidential correspondence among the justices, meaning their private back and forth,
sentences.zh: 嗯，《纽约时报》获得并发布了16页大法官之间的机密通信，也就是他们私下的往来，

sentences.en: that reveal the origins of the shadow docket.
sentences.zh: 揭示了“影子案卷”的起源。

sentences.en: Through these papers,
sentences.zh: 通过这些文件，

sentences.en: we can eavesdrop on the justices at the exact moment that they are abandoning time-tested norms of judicial procedure and backing themselves into a new way of doing business.
sentences.zh: 我们可以在大法官们放弃久经考验的司法程序规范，并把自己逼入一种新的工作方式的那个确切时刻，窃听他们。

sentences.en: That new way being the shadow docket.
sentences.zh: 那种新的方式就是“影子案卷”。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, Adam, give us the context for these documents that Jody just mentioned.
sentences.zh: 那么，亚当，给我们介绍一下乔迪刚才提到的这些文件的背景。

sentences.en: So, these documents concern a case in 2016 arising from President Obama's Clean Power Plan.
sentences.zh: 这些文件涉及2016年奥巴马总统的《清洁电力计划》引发的一起案件。

sentences.en: The Clean Power Plan, you may recall, was Obama's attempt late in his second term to do something about climate change.
sentences.zh: 你可能还记得，《清洁电力计划》是奥巴马在第二个任期末期为应对气候变化所做的尝试。

sentences.en: He'd failed to get legislation through Congress.
sentences.zh: 他未能让立法通过国会。

sentences.en: He instructed the EPA to issue regulations.
sentences.zh: 他指示环保署发布法规。

sentences.en: And these regulations would fundamentally shift the American power system away from coal and toward cleaner sources of energy.
sentences.zh: 这些法规将从根本上改变美国的电力系统，使其从煤炭转向更清洁的能源。

sentences.en: This, of course, drove industry crazy and red states crazy.
sentences.zh: 这当然让工业界和红州（共和党州）抓狂了。

sentences.en: And they challenged it.
sentences.zh: 他们对此提出了挑战。

sentences.en: And that's not surprising.
sentences.zh: 这并不令人惊讶。

sentences.en: And they go to the D.C.
sentences.zh: 他们去了哥伦比亚特区巡回法院，要求两件事。

sentences.en: circuit and they ask for two things.
sentences.zh: 第一，他们最大的要求是请裁定《清洁电力计划》不合法，未经国会授权。

sentences.en: One, their big ask is to please hold this Clean Power Plan unlawful, unauthorized by Congress.
sentences.zh: 但第二，他们要求，在此期间，请停止它。

sentences.en: But second, they ask, in the meantime, please halt it.
sentences.zh: 不要让它生效。

sentences.en: Don't let it go into place.
sentences.zh: 在诉讼进行期间，你们要暂时冻结它。

sentences.en: You'll freeze it for the time being while the litigation goes forward.
sentences.zh: 哥伦比亚特区巡回法院说，关于第一点，我们将安排快速辩论。

sentences.en: And the D.C.
sentences.zh: 我们将准备好就该计划是否违法给你们一个答案。

sentences.en: circuit says, on the first point, we'll set it down for a quick argument.
sentences.zh: 不过，关于第二点，我们不会暂停它。

sentences.en: And we'll get ourselves in position to give you an answer on whether the program is illegal or not.
sentences.zh: 我们将让该计划开始实施。

sentences.en: On the second thing, though, we're not going to pause it.
sentences.zh: 然后挑战者，即各州和商业团体，做了一件不同寻常的事情。

sentences.en: We're going to let the program start.
sentences.zh: 他们去了最高法院，说，在任何下级法院考虑《清洁电力计划》的合法性之前，他们对最高法院说，请停止这个计划。

sentences.en: And then the challengers, the states and business groups, do something unusual.
sentences.zh: 请在诉讼通过哥伦比亚特区巡回法院、回到最高法院期间冻结它。

sentences.en: They go to the Supreme Court and say, before any lower court has considered the lawfulness of the Clean Power Plan, they say to the Supreme Court, please halt this.
sentences.zh: 在此期间，《清洁电力计划》不应该实施。

sentences.en: Please freeze this for as long as it takes for this litigation to go through the D.C.
sentences.zh: 案件中涉及的每个人都知道这是一个前所未有的请求。

sentences.en: circuit, back up to the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 乔迪，这个来自那些不希望奥巴马政府的《清洁电力计划》存活下来的人的前所未有的请求，

sentences.en: In the meantime, the Clean Power Plan should not be happening.
sentences.zh: 送达最高法院时，如果我没记错的话，当时法院的立场相当平均。

sentences.en: And everybody involved in the case knew that this was an unprecedented requeSt.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And, Jody, this unprecedented request by those who do not want the Clean Power Plan from the Obama administration to survive
sentences.zh: 这是一个5比4的法院，倾向于共和党任命的大法官。

sentences.en: arrives at a Supreme Court, if memory serves, that's pretty evenly split at the moment.
sentences.zh: 但那个时代的人说，当时的最高法院真的不同。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 它充满了辩论。

sentences.en: It's a 5-4 court that leans towards Republican-appointed justices.
sentences.zh: 安东尼·肯尼迪大法官是共和党任命的，但他也是摇摆票。

sentences.en: But people from that era say the Supreme Court was really different back then.
sentences.zh: 那个时代有人称他为，引用一下，“可说服的人”。

sentences.en: It was alive with debate.
sentences.zh: 你永远不知道他到底会站在哪一边。

sentences.en: Justice Anthony Kennedy was a Republican appointee, but he was also the swing vote.
sentences.zh: 就在此之前，他曾对同性婚姻投了赞成票。

sentences.en: And somebody from that era called him a, quote, persuadable person.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You never knew exactly which way he would come out.
sentences.zh: 尽管他是共和党任命的，但他最终成为了该案中令人惊讶的决定性一票。

sentences.en: And just before this, he had said yes to gay marriage.
sentences.zh: 总之，这是一个不可预测的最高法院，很多事情都有可能发生。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Even though he was a Republican appointee, he ends up being the somewhat surprising, decisive vote in that case.
sentences.zh: 那么，亚当，这个立场相当平均的法院对这个紧急请求有何反应？

sentences.en: All to say this is a unpredictable Supreme Court where a lot of things are possible.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它送达了首席大法官约翰·罗伯茨的办公室。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 他是负责哥伦比亚特区巡回法院的大法官。

sentences.en: So how does this very evenly split court react, Adam, to this emergency request?
sentences.zh: 所以这些事情首先会交给他。

sentences.en: Well, it arrives in the chambers of Chief Justice John Roberts.
sentences.zh: 在通常情况下，案件涉及的律师预期的结果是，他会简单地拒绝它，拒绝申请，

sentences.en: He's the justice who oversees the D.C.
sentences.zh: 或者可能把它发给他的同事，然后他们会集体拒绝它。

sentences.en: circuit.
So these things go to him in the first instance.
sentences.zh: 所以这些东西首先会送到他那里。

sentences.en: And in the ordinary course, what the lawyers involved in the case expected would happen was that he would simply deny it, deny the application,
sentences.zh: 按照惯例，涉案律师们预料会发生的情况是，他会直接拒绝，驳回申请，

sentences.en: or maybe send it to his colleagues and they would collectively deny it.
sentences.zh: 或者转交给他的同事，然后他们会集体驳回。

sentences.en: But what he does instead is he starts writing a memo telling the other justices that they should take this very seriously.
sentences.zh: 但他采取的做法是写了一份备忘录，告诉其他大法官，他们应该非常严肃地对待这件事。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And that sets off a five-day sprint in which the justices are going to revise centuries of Supreme Court practice.
sentences.zh: 这引发了一场为期五天的冲刺，大法官们将在此期间彻底改变最高法院沿袭了几个世纪的惯例。

sentences.en: I'm Wynna Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是 Wynna Liu。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我负责编写《纽约时报》游戏中的“Connections”谜题。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我还喜欢试图捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是 Sam Mazursky，我每天负责制作“Spelling Bee”和“Letterboxd”游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做联觉的特质。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由真人制作的，就像你们刚才听到的这些人一样。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com/games 即可开始游玩。

sentences.en: So Adam and Jodi, we're now in the phase of this story where the justices are exchanging these memos that you have unearthed over these five days.
sentences.zh: 那么 Adam 和 Jodi，我们现在进入了这个故事的阶段，大法官们正在交换你们在这五天里挖掘出来的这些备忘录。

sentences.en: And Adam, let's start with this opening salvo from the Chief Justice, John Roberts.
sentences.zh: Adam，我们先从首席大法官约翰·罗伯茨（John Roberts）的开场白开始吧。

sentences.en: Tell us about his first memo.
sentences.zh: 跟我们讲讲他的第一份备忘录。

sentences.en: So this is a three-page, single-spaced memo on letterhead that says the chambers of the Chief Justice.
sentences.zh: 这是一份三页纸、单倍行距的备忘录，抬头写着“首席大法官办公室”。

sentences.en: And he explains to his colleagues why he thinks the Obama plan needs to be halted.
sentences.zh: 他在备忘录中向同事们解释了为什么他认为奥巴马的计划必须被叫停。

sentences.en: He says it's going to impose enormous burdens on states and on the coal industry.
sentences.zh: 他说这会给各州和煤炭行业带来巨大的负担。

sentences.en: He says there's no time to waste because they're going to have to start complying with the requirements of the Clean Power Plan right away.
sentences.zh: 他说刻不容缓，因为他们必须立即开始遵守《清洁电力计划》的要求。

sentences.en: He says that the law the president relies on to authorize this move, the Clean Air Act of 1970, does not clearly give him that power.
sentences.zh: 他说总统授权此举所依据的法律——1970年的《清洁空气法》——并没有明确赋予他这种权力。

sentences.en: And the court likes to say that unless a president clearly has the power, it runs afoul of the major questions doctrine and is no good.
sentences.zh: 法院向来喜欢说，除非总统拥有明确的权力，否则就违反了“重大问题原则”，是行不通的。

sentences.en: And he says the EPA has kind of tricked us not long ago, and we're not going to let him do that to us again.
sentences.zh: 他还说，环保署（EPA）不久前耍了我们一次，我们绝不会让他们再耍我们第二次。

sentences.en: Tricked how?
sentences.zh: 怎么耍的？

sentences.en: What does he say?
sentences.zh: 他说了什么？

sentences.en: Just a few months before all of this, the court had ruled against the EPA in a case involving mercury emissions.
sentences.zh: 就在这一切发生的前几个月，法院在涉及汞排放的案件中做出了不利于环保署的裁决。

sentences.en: That case had been litigated over three years, three and a half years.
sentences.zh: 那个案子打了三年，三年半的时间。

sentences.en: The normal Supreme Court process.
sentences.zh: 那是正常的最高法院审理程序。

sentences.en: In the normal Supreme Court process.
sentences.zh: 在正常的最高法院程序中。

sentences.en: And nobody had granted the challengers a stay.
sentences.zh: 而且没有人批准挑战方的暂缓执行请求。

sentences.en: So they were starting to comply with the regulation as the litigation goes forward.
sentences.zh: 所以他们在诉讼进行的同时，就开始遵守该法规了。

sentences.en: The Supreme Court rules against the EPA.
sentences.zh: 最高法院做出了不利于环保署的裁决。

sentences.en: And the next day, the EPA official puts up a blog post and essentially says, very nicely ruled against this Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 第二天，环保署的一名官员发布了一篇博客文章，基本上说，最高法院这次裁决得真好。

sentences.en: But in the meantime, the rule has essentially gone into effect.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，该规则实际上已经生效了。

sentences.en: And your ruling doesn't mean very much.
sentences.zh: 你们的裁决并没有什么实际意义。

sentences.en: And that seems to drive the chief justice crazy.
sentences.zh: 这似乎让首席大法官抓狂了。

sentences.en: He concludes at the end of the memo, the absence of a stay in that Mercury case allowed the agency to effectively implement an important program we held to be contrary to law.
sentences.zh: 他在备忘录末尾总结道，在那起汞排放案中，由于没有暂缓执行，导致该机构得以有效地实施了一个我们认定违反法律的重要计划。

sentences.en: And you have the sense that he's peeved, he's irked, and he's not going to let it happen again.
sentences.zh: 你能感觉到他很恼火，很生气，他绝不会让这种情况再次发生。

sentences.en: Robert is telling his fellow justices in this memo, I don't like what I am seeing from the Obama administration when it comes to its efforts to regulate climate change.
sentences.zh: 罗伯茨在这份备忘录中告诉其他大法官，我不喜欢奥巴马政府在监管气候变化方面的所作所为。

sentences.en: I think they're being sneaky.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他们很狡猾。

sentences.en: And the traditional slow legal process is letting them be kind of sneaky when it comes to these regulations.
sentences.zh: 而传统的缓慢法律程序让他们在这些法规上显得有些狡猾。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And the chief justice may be right that, in retrospect, they should have paused the Mercury plan, which was pretty fast moving.
sentences.zh: 首席大法官说得或许没错，回想起来，他们当时确实应该暂停那个进展相当迅速的汞排放计划。

sentences.en: But when you think about the clean power plan, it's less clear that the court needs to act faSt.
sentences.zh: 但当你想到《清洁电力计划》时，法院是否需要迅速采取行动就不那么明确了。

sentences.en: And Justice Breyer says as much in a memo he writes, responding to Roberts that same day.
sentences.zh: 布雷耶（Breyer）大法官在当天写给罗伯茨的回复备忘录中也表达了同样的观点。

sentences.en: He lays out the chronology of the Clean Power Plan, which doesn't require industry to do anything for six years.
sentences.zh: 他列出了《清洁电力计划》的时间表，该计划在六年内不需要行业做任何事情。

sentences.en: And doesn't require total compliance until 2030.
sentences.zh: 并且直到2030年才要求完全合规。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's 2016, so that's quite some time.
sentences.zh: 现在是2016年，所以还有相当长的时间。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So he's taking a completely different attitude than Roberts.
sentences.zh: 所以他采取的态度与罗伯茨完全不同。

sentences.en: He's thinking there's plenty of time to do this in the usual course.
sentences.zh: 他认为有充足的时间按常规流程来处理这件事。

sentences.en: And he doesn't know why the court should be doing what he says is quite unusual.
sentences.zh: 而且他不明白为什么法院要采取他所说的“非常不寻常”的做法。

sentences.en: He says it's unusual for the court to issue a state of an agency's order during the time that the Court of Appeals is considering its lawfulness.
sentences.zh: 他说，在联邦上诉法院审理其合法性期间，法院发布暂缓执行行政命令是不寻常的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: As you mentioned earlier, the D.C.
sentences.zh: 正如你刚才提到的，哥伦比亚特区巡回法院正在审理此案。

sentences.en: court, the circuit court, is looking at this.
sentences.zh: 巡回法院正在审理此案。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So he's saying, let it play out.
sentences.zh: 所以他的意思是，让它按程序走吧。

sentences.en: He doesn't understand what the rush is.
sentences.zh: 他不明白为什么要这么着急。

sentences.en: And he would issue an order that basically says, D.C.
sentences.zh: 他会发布一项命令，基本上就是说，特区巡回法院，继续你们的工作吧。

sentences.en: circuit, get on with your business.
sentences.zh: 其他人，如果遇到问题，再回来找我们。

sentences.en: Everybody else, if you run into problems, come back to us.
sentences.zh: 最有趣的是首席大法官的反应。

sentences.en: What's so interesting is the chief justice's reaction.
sentences.zh: 他第二天就写信回击了。

sentences.en: He writes right back the next day.
sentences.zh: 他的语气发生了一些变化。

sentences.en: And his tone changes a little bit.
sentences.zh: 他似乎变得更加恼火了。

sentences.en: He seems to be getting more irritated.
sentences.zh: 他非常坚持法院必须继续推进并阻止这一计划。

sentences.en: He's very insistent that the court needs to go ahead and block this.
sentences.zh: 我想特别读一下他的一段话。

sentences.en: And I want to read you one quote of his in particular.
sentences.zh: 他说，我承认这次暂缓执行请求的程序并不典型，

sentences.en: He says, I recognize that the posture of this stay request is not typical,
sentences.zh: 但我们正在审查的，被描述为电力行业有史以来最昂贵的法规。

sentences.en: but review is sought of what has been described as the most expensive regulation ever imposed on the power sector.
sentences.zh: 让我们翻译一下这句话。

sentences.en: So let's translate that.
sentences.zh: 他在第一句话里，直接驳回了他同事对程序的担忧。

sentences.en: He, in that first phrase, is just dismissing his colleagues' procedural concern.
sentences.zh: 布雷耶大法官说，嘿，这真的很不寻常。

sentences.en: Justice Breyer is saying, hey, this is really unusual.
sentences.zh: 好像这事儿有什么不合规的地方。

sentences.en: Like there's something irregular about this.
sentences.zh: 而首席大法官基本上是在说，我知道，我知道，我知道，

sentences.en: And the chief justice is saying, essentially, I know, I know, I know,
sentences.zh: 但这不重要，因为这项法规对各州和煤炭行业来说太昂贵了，我们必须采取行动。

sentences.en: but it doesn't matter because this regulation is so expensive for states and the coal industry that we have to do something.
sentences.zh: 所以，这份备忘录中流露出的不耐烦，实际上是因为首席大法官已经准备好现在就做出裁决了。

sentences.en: And so the sense of impatience that runs through this memo is really animated by the fact that the chief justice, he's ready to rule now.
sentences.zh: 他认为法院会批准复审。

sentences.en: He thinks the court is going to grant review.
sentences.zh: 他认为法院会推翻这个《清洁电力计划》。

sentences.en: He thinks the court is going to strike down this clean power plan.
sentences.zh: 他不明白为什么要让程序走完，因为他今天就已经知道结果了。

sentences.en: And he doesn't understand why you need to let the process run out because he knows what the answer is today.
sentences.zh: 他甚至写道，他相信如果法院在未来的某个日期真正审理此案的实质内容，该法律“极不可能”存续。

sentences.en: He even writes that he believes if the court were to ultimately at some future date hear the case on the merits for real, the law would be, quote, highly unlikely to survive.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，首席大法官是在说，在没有经过最高法院审理案件、审议等任何正常程序的情况下，他已经下定决心了。

sentences.en: In other words, the chief justice is saying, without going through any of the normal process of how the Supreme Court reviews a case, deliberates, he's made up his mind.
sentences.zh: 这个法院将会做出不利于该法规的裁决。

sentences.en: And this court is going to find against this regulation.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 这份备忘录还揭示了一点，那就是他又提到了环保署。

sentences.en: And what's also revealing about this memo is that he mentions the EPA again.
sentences.zh: 再次说明，这份备忘录清楚地表明，他确实与奥巴马政府处于权力斗争之中。

sentences.en: Again, this memo makes it clear that he is truly in a power struggle with the Obama administration.
sentences.zh: 他觉得这个机构试图将法院边缘化，他不希望这种情况再次发生。

sentences.en: He feels this agency has tried to sideline the court and he does not want it to happen again.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 他用了很多话来表达这一点。

sentences.en: And he says that in so many words.
sentences.zh: 他说，我认为，一项旨在改变国家经济很大一部分的规则，在被当作既成事实提出之前，应该先由本院进行审查。

sentences.en: He says, I am of the mind that a rule decided to transform a substantial swath of the nation's economy should be tested by this court before it is presented as a fait accompli.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在公开场合，我们习惯看到首席大法官表现出非常公正、庄重的态度。

sentences.en: You know, in public, we're used to seeing the chief justice strike a very even-handed, magisterial tone.
sentences.zh: 在这里，他表现得像个推土机。

sentences.en: Here, he's acting as a bulldozer.
sentences.zh: 他在对同事们说，我们应该做一些我们从未做过的事情，而且我们应该快点做。

sentences.en: He's saying to his colleagues, we should do something we have never done before and we should do it faSt.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 然后，同样由民主党任命的埃琳娜·卡根（Elena Kagan）大法官敲响了警钟。

sentences.en: And then Justice Elena Kagan, also a Democratic appointee, sounds an alarm.
sentences.zh: 她提交了一份备忘录，反对首席大法官的立场，措辞更加直接。

sentences.en: She files a memo opposing the chief's stance that is even more direct.
sentences.zh: 她说，这些申请中寻求的救济的独特性质让我感到非常迟疑。

sentences.en: She says, the unique nature of the relief sought in these applications gives me real pause.
sentences.zh: 她用“史无前例”这个词来形容首席大法官想要做的事情。

sentences.en: She uses the word unprecedented to describe what the chief wants to do.
sentences.zh: 她还说，我们需要更多时间来处理这个案子。

sentences.en: And she also says, we need more time on this case.
sentences.zh: 这很复杂。

sentences.en: This is complicated.
sentences.zh: 她写道，从实质上讲，这是一个涉及复杂法律和监管制度的棘手案件。

sentences.en: She writes, on the merits, this is a difficult case involving a complex statutory and regulatory regime.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，她是在说，这太奇怪了。

sentences.en: So, in other words, she's saying, this is weird.
sentences.zh: 我们确定要这么做吗？

sentences.en: Are we sure we want to do this?
sentences.zh: 根据这些备忘录，所有相关人员开始意识到这件事的严重性。

sentences.en: The gravity of this all is, based on these memos, starting to dawn on everybody involved.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 记住，迈克尔，这件事进展得有多快。

sentences.en: And remember, Michael, how fast this is moving.
sentences.zh: 我们现在才讨论这个影响深远的案件仅仅三天。

sentences.en: We are now only three days into this discussion of this hugely consequential case.
sentences.zh: 接下来要说的是共和党任命的大法官塞缪尔·阿利托（Samuel Alito）。

sentences.en: And the next person to speak of is Justice Samuel Alito, a Republican appointee.
sentences.zh: 他说，如果法院不采取行动，将损害其自身的合法性，这可是个大问题。

sentences.en: And he says that if the court fails to act, it'll do damage to its own legitimacy, which is, you know, quite a big thing to say.
sentences.zh: 他说，未能暂缓执行该规则，威胁到我们提供有意义的司法审查的能力，进而威胁到我们的机构合法性，使其化为乌有。

sentences.en: He says, a failure to stay this rule threatens to render our ability to provide meaningful judicial review and, by extension, our institutional legitimacy, a nullity.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们不仅意识到法院内部存在真正的冲突，不仅意识到他们正在朝着不同的方向前进，

sentences.en: So, not only is it dawning on them that there's a real clash in the court, not only is it dawning on them that they're moving in a different direction,
sentences.zh: 他们还将此事——至少阿利托大法官是这样——描述为对法院本身几乎是存在性的威胁。

sentences.en: they're also portraying this thing, or at least Justice Alito is, as an almost existential threat to the court itself.
sentences.zh: 所以，你可以看出阿利托大法官在呼应首席大法官那种被冒犯的感觉。

sentences.en: So, you can see there that Justice Alito is echoing the Chief Justice's sense of insult.
sentences.zh: 首席大法官觉得被奥巴马政府和环保署耍了。

sentences.en: The Chief Justice feels played by the Obama administration, the EPA.
sentences.zh: 而阿利托大法官则说，看，奥巴马政府正试图边缘化我们，让我们变得无关紧要。

sentences.en: And Justice Alito is saying, look, the Obama administration is trying to sideline us, to render us irrelevant.
sentences.zh: Adam，我感到震惊的是，首席大法官和阿利托大法官描述的因素，实际上与法律无关，对吧？

sentences.en: Adam, I'm struck by the fact that both the Chief Justice and Justice Alito are describing factors that are not really about the law, right?
sentences.zh: 它们与宪法无关。

sentences.en: They're not about the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 他们似乎更关注对奥巴马政府的不满，对最高法院地位的担忧，以及合法性问题。

sentences.en: They seem to be rather focused on their grievances with the Obama administration, their fears about the place of the Supreme Court, questions of legitimacy.
sentences.zh: 而这些并不是我认为在法律层面上推动决策的因素。

sentences.en: And those are not factors that I think of as, legally speaking, animating a decision.
sentences.zh: 但这就是这些文件如此非凡之处。

sentences.en: But that's what's so extraordinary about these papers.
sentences.zh: 它们打开了一扇窗，让我们看到大法官们是如何交谈的，他们对于自己的真实议程是多么坦率。

sentences.en: They open a window on how the justices talk to each other, how frank they are, really, about their actual agendas.
sentences.zh: 因此，它们与他们平时的裁决截然不同，平时的裁决就像一种面具，将法院描绘成局限于事实、

sentences.en: And so, they're quite different in kind from their ordinary decisions, which are a kind of mask that portray the court as confining itself to the facts,
sentences.zh: 相关的法律材料，并暗示他们得出了必然的法律结果。

sentences.en: the relevant legal materials, and suggesting that they produce an inevitable legal result.
sentences.zh: 然而，大法官们也是人，他们生活在这个世界上，他们会考虑很多事情。

sentences.en: Whereas, the justices are human beings, and they live in the world, and they take account of a lot of stuff.
sentences.zh: 他们不在公开场合说，但事实证明他们在私下里会说。

sentences.en: They don't say it in public, but it turns out they say it in private.
sentences.zh: 好的，接下来发生了什么？

sentences.en: Okay, and what happens next?
sentences.zh: 正如预测的那样，整件事归结于摇摆票安东尼·肯尼迪（Anthony Kennedy）大法官。

sentences.en: So, the whole thing, as predicted, comes down to Justice Anthony Kennedy, the swing vote.
sentences.zh: 在2月9日，辩论的第五天，他发了一张非常简短的便条。

sentences.en: And on February 9th, the fifth day of the debate, he sends a very short note.
sentences.zh: 上面几乎没说什么。

sentences.en: It doesn't say much at all.
sentences.zh: 只有三句话，他说他投票支持首席大法官，仅此而已。

sentences.en: It's three sentences, he says he's voting with the chief, and that's it.
sentences.zh: 结束了。

sentences.en: It's over.
sentences.zh: 最高法院以五比四的投票结果做出裁决，几小时内，最高法院就发布了命令。

sentences.en: The Supreme Court rules five to four, and within hours, the Supreme Court issues its order.
sentences.zh: 与我们刚才告诉你们的所有私下辩论相比，这只有一段话。

sentences.en: In contrast to all this private debate that we've just told you about, it's just one paragraph.
sentences.zh: 这是法律上的套话。

sentences.en: It's legal boilerplate.
sentences.zh: 没有任何解释。

sentences.en: There is no explanation.
sentences.zh: 法院所说的只是他们正在阻止奥巴马总统标志性的环保倡议。

sentences.en: All the court says is that they are blocking President Obama's signature environmental initiative.
sentences.zh: 所以，这真的是一个要问你们两个的问题。

sentences.en: So, this is really a question to both of you.
sentences.zh: 既然你们已经能够撬开这个之前被锁住的“影子案卷”诞生的盒子，既然你们已经深入到了这个新时代第一个真正的案件内部，

sentences.en: Now that you have been able to pry open this previously locked box of the birth of the shadow docket, now that you've gotten inside the first real case of this new era,
sentences.zh: 你们从所见所闻中最终得出了什么结论？

sentences.en: what do you ultimately conclude from what you've seen?
sentences.zh: 影子案卷的批评者一直担心，在这种时间压力下，没有充分的简报、辩论和审议，法院无法做出最好的工作。

sentences.en: Critics of the shadow docket have always feared that the court can't do its best work under this kind of time pressure without good briefing and arguments and deliberation.
sentences.zh: 而这些备忘录证实了这种批评。

sentences.en: And these memos vindicate that criticism.
sentences.zh: 这不是法院在做A+级的工作。

sentences.en: This is not the court doing A-plus work.
sentences.zh: 这是法院在抛出各种想法，

sentences.en: This is the court throwing ideas around,
sentences.zh: 似乎是出于对一些保守派视为激进的总统的不满，

sentences.en: seeming to be motivated by grievances against a president that some of the conservatives view as activist,
sentences.zh: 彼此之间变得尖酸刻薄，总体上没有做我们与国家最高法院联系在一起的那种工作。

sentences.en: getting snippy with each other and just in general not doing the kind of work we associate with the nation's highest court.
sentences.zh: 所以，人们认为影子案卷是有问题的，因为法院在信息不足的情况下行动太快了。

sentences.en: So, people think the shadow docket is problematic because the court is moving too fast on not enough information.
sentences.zh: 而这些备忘录支持了这种批评。

sentences.en: And these memos support that criticism.
sentences.zh: 接着Adam的想法说，他们不仅是在裁决一个非常重要的案件。

sentences.en: And to continue Adam's thought, they're not only deciding a very important case.
sentences.zh: 他们正在决定的是一种全新的工作方式。

sentences.en: What they're deciding on is a whole new way of doing business.
sentences.zh: 他们正在决定的是一种全新的工作方式。

sentences.en: They are disregarding time-tested procedures that have kept courts upright for a very long time.
sentences.zh: 他们无视了那些长期以来确保法院公正运行的、经受住时间考验的程序。

sentences.en: And they don't seem to be considering the implications.
sentences.zh: 而且他们似乎并没有考虑其带来的影响。

sentences.en: It's true that Justice Kagan calls what the court is doing unprecedented, but nobody goes further and asks the question, well, if we do this, where is it going to lead?
sentences.zh: 诚然，卡根大法官称法院目前的做法史无前例，但没有人进一步追问：如果我们这样做，会导致什么后果？

sentences.en: And where it leads is what we've seen over the first year plus of the Trump administration, where the court is deluged by emergency applications
sentences.zh: 而后果正如我们在特朗普政府执政一年多以来所见，法院被紧急申请淹没，

sentences.en: and is spending seemingly half its time on them and is often in very short periods of time ruling for the Trump administration on major questions like immigration,
sentences.zh: 似乎将一半的时间都花在这些申请上，并且经常在极短的时间内就移民等重大问题做出有利于特朗普政府的裁决，

sentences.en: like agency power, like government spending, like transgender troops.
sentences.zh: 比如机构权力、政府支出、跨性别军人等问题。

sentences.en: And in contrast to the Obama experience where the court shut down a major presidential initiative, these days on the shadow docket, the court is mostly and indeed overwhelmingly
sentences.zh: 与奥巴马时期法院叫停总统重大倡议的经历相比，如今在“影子案卷”上，法院大多时候，甚至可以说绝大多数时候，

sentences.en: allowing President Trump's initiatives to go forward.
sentences.zh: 都在放行特朗普总统的倡议。

sentences.en: So should we consider the shadow docket as encouraging the justices' most partisan instincts?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们是否应该认为“影子案卷”助长了大法官们最偏袒的本能？

sentences.en: Political scientists will tell you that there's more partisan voting on the shadow docket than on the merits docket.
sentences.zh: 政治学家会告诉你，在“影子案卷”上的投票比在“实质案卷”上更具党派色彩。

sentences.en: That you're much more likely to see Republican appointees voting in favor of a Republican president
sentences.zh: 你更有可能看到共和党任命的大法官投票支持共和党总统，

sentences.en: and against a Democratic president than on the court's usual docket, than on its merits docket.
sentences.zh: 而反对民主党总统，这比法院通常的案卷，即实质案卷的情况要多得多。

sentences.en: And one example of why this is so and why people, when they're acting fast, might rely on their partisan impulses is in the Biden years.
sentences.zh: 为什么会这样，以及为什么人们在匆忙行事时可能会依赖党派冲动，拜登执政期间就是一个例子。

sentences.en: The court voted against Biden on three different emergency applications, which then eventually returned to the court.
sentences.zh: 法院在三项不同的紧急申请中投票反对拜登，这些案件后来最终又回到了法院。

sentences.en: And the court, when it had a chance to do the full thing, to actually give it consideration and deliberation, voted for Biden in those three merits cases.
sentences.zh: 而当法院有机会进行全面审理，真正给予考虑和审议时，它在这些实质案件中投票支持了拜登。

sentences.en: So in short, the more time the court has to consider cases,
sentences.zh: 简而言之，法院审理案件的时间越充裕，

sentences.en: the more its partisan impulses are dampened.
sentences.zh: 其党派冲动就越会被抑制。

sentences.en: Deliberation also produces trust in the court, and that's the second part.
sentences.zh: 审议也能建立对法院的信任，这是第二点。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Public truSt.
sentences.zh: 公众信任。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The elected branches get legitimacy because of elections, right?
sentences.zh: 民选部门因为选举而获得合法性，对吧？

sentences.en: We choose our leaders, but we don't choose our Supreme Court justices, and they stay in power for a very long time.
sentences.zh: 我们选择我们的领导人，但我们不选择最高法院大法官，而且他们任职的时间非常长。

sentences.en: Their entire lives.
sentences.zh: 终身制。

sentences.en: And so the act of writing an opinion for a judge is the act of saying, here's why you should trust me.
sentences.zh: 所以，法官撰写判决书的行为，就是在说：这就是你应该信任我的原因。

sentences.en: Even if you disagree with this outcome,
sentences.zh: 即使你不同意这个结果，

sentences.en: I'm going to show you my work.
sentences.zh: 我也会向你展示我的论证过程。

sentences.en: I'm going to show you how I got to my answer.
sentences.zh: 我会向你展示我是如何得出结论的。

sentences.en: And so when the Supreme Court changes its way of operating and does that so much less, there is truly a risk to the legitimacy of the institution.
sentences.zh: 因此，当最高法院改变其运作方式，且大幅减少这种做法时，该机构的合法性确实面临风险。

sentences.en: And recall that the Supreme Court's public approval ratings, the public's trust in the court, is testing all-time lows.
sentences.zh: 请记住，最高法院的公众支持率，即公众对法院的信任度，正处于历史最低点。

sentences.en: And its increasing reliance on the shadow docket to make major decisions is only going to make that problem worse.
sentences.zh: 而它越来越依赖“影子案卷”来做出重大决定，只会让这个问题变得更糟。

sentences.en: Well, Adam and Jodi, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，亚当和乔迪，非常感谢你们。

sentences.en: Thank you, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，迈克尔。

sentences.en: Thanks, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢，迈克尔。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.zh: 周日，特朗普总统和伊朗甚至无法就本周是否会举行新一轮和平谈判达成一致。

sentences.zh: 将于今晚返回巴基斯坦进行谈判。

sentences.zh: 但几个小时后，伊朗表示并未同意这些会谈。

sentences.zh: 这种反复无常的情况概括了周末令人眼花缭乱的事态发展。

sentences.zh: 在以色列宣布与真主党达成停火协议后，

sentences.zh: 伊朗表示将重新开放霍尔木兹海峡。

sentences.en: But it then tightened its grip over the waterway, in retaliation, it said, for a week-old U.S.
sentences.zh: 但随后它又加强了对该水道的控制，称这是为了报复美国为期一周的

sentences.en: naval blockade.
sentences.zh: 海军封锁。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, on Sunday night, a U.S.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，周日晚上，一艘美国

sentences.en: Navy destroyer attacked an Iranian cargo ship that had allegedly defied that blockade.
sentences.zh: 海军驱逐舰袭击了一艘据称无视该封锁的伊朗货船。

sentences.en: And...
sentences.zh: 而且……

sentences.zh: 这是一个悲剧性的情况，也许是你所经历过的最糟糕的悲剧。

sentences.zh: 路易斯安那州的一名枪手杀害了八名儿童，当地警方称这是一起家庭暴力案件。
